title: Point of Maximum Interval Overlap
statement:
You are given `n` closed intervals `[l[i], r[i]]` with integer endpoints; interval `i` contains every integer `x` with `l[i] ≤ x ≤ r[i]`, endpoints included.

For an integer point `x`, its **overlap** is the number of intervals that contain `x`. Find the integer point whose overlap is the **maximum possible**. If several points reach that maximum, print the **smallest** (first) one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `l[i]` and `r[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the smallest point whose overlap is maximum.

examples.explanation: Points 2, 3 and 4 lie in two intervals (the first and the second); points 5 and 6 also lie in two (the second and the third). No point lies in all three. The maximum overlap is 2, first reached at point 2.
Point 3 has overlap 1, points 7 and 9 have overlap 1, and point 8 lies in both [7, 9] and [8, 8], so its overlap is 2. The answer is 8.

hints: The coordinates go up to 10^9, so you cannot count overlaps for every integer. The overlap only changes at interval endpoints.
Turn each interval into two events: +1 at `l` and -1 at `r + 1` (the first point that no longer contains it). Sort the events by position and sweep through them keeping a running count.
Apply every event at the same position before looking at the count, and only record a new best when the count is strictly larger than the previous best. That keeps the smallest point on ties.
